name: Collect specimens and ECGs in long-term care and retirement homes
sector: medical laboratory and health services (community laboratory)
summary: Residents of long-term care and retirement homes are often too frail to visit a collection centre, so the laboratory sends mobile lab assistants on early-morning runs to draw blood, pick up other specimens and record ECGs at the bedside. At each home the assistant checks the list with the charge nurse, identifies each resident with staff help, draws and labels the tubes, documents the collection and hands the cooled specimens to a courier within the processing window. Residents with dementia who refuse or are agitated, residents who are asleep or not fasting and fragile veins cause missed draws that must be reported and rebooked.

baseline.org_archetype: The mobile services division of a large Canadian community laboratory, with about 120 mobile lab assistants serving long-term care and retirement homes in Ontario and Manitoba on daily runs.
baseline.notes: One case is one resident's collection on the day's schedule. Building the schedule and entering orders belongs to the scheduling process; courier transport, accessioning and ECG reading are separate processes. In 2020-2022 infection-control screening and outbreak restrictions added time at each home.

trigger: The resident appears on the day's collection schedule for a home, with a requisition and labels printed.
end_state: The resident's labelled specimens are handed to the courier (and any ECG transmitted), or the collection is recorded as cancelled or missed and rebooked or held.

volume.seasonality: Steady through the year, with more draws in winter respiratory and outbreak seasons and fewer on holidays; Monday and Tuesday runs are heavier because few homes are visited at weekends.

evidence.note: Taken from the organisation file's driver (18,000 to 30,000 a month), itself an estimate built on Ontario's 626 homes and 78,000 residents (fao2019).

roles.title: Mobile laboratory assistant (long-term care, retirement homes and house calls)

evidence.note: Certified health professionals do mobile blood and ECG collections in long-term care and retirement homes (dyn_services). FTE: about 88 of the 120 mobile assistants, close to hands-on time (about 28 minutes per resident including the travel share and ECGs) times 24,000 collections; the rest do house calls. Wage near the Job Bank 33101 Ontario median; Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

Team leads cover absent assistants' homes and handle on-the-day problems; share of the 8 team leads is an estimate. Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

Schedulers reschedule missed and cancelled collections reported from the run; building the daily schedule belongs to the scheduling process. Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

roles.title: Mobile services regional manager
roles.department: Mobile and home collection (The model laboratory Mobile Services)

evidence.note: Regional managers resolve homes' complaints about missed or late collections; estimate. Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

systems.name: Laboratory information system (orders, accessioning, results, autoverification rules)
Courier routing, dispatch and web-based order and tracking system
Printed daily collection list, requisitions and LIS specimen labels
Portable 12-lead ECG recorder with transmission to the reading service
Mobile phone (calls and texts with the scheduling desk and couriers)

steps.name: Pick up the day's list, requisitions and labels
steps.description: Before the run the mobile lab assistant collects or prints the day's collection list for each home, the requisitions and the LIS barcode labels for every resident, checks that tubes, butterfly needles, tourniquets, coolers with cold packs and, if ECGs are booked, the ECG recorder and electrodes are stocked, and plans the order of homes so fasting draws come first.

error.defect_description: A label set or requisition is missing from the pack, found only at the bedside.

evidence.note: Per-resident share of preparing a daily run of about 15 to 25 residents; the wait is from the schedule being issued the afternoon before to the early-morning start, longer over weekends. Estimates.

steps.name: Cover an absent assistant's homes
steps.description: When an assistant calls in sick, the team lead redistributes that assistant's homes among the others on shift or goes out personally, phones the homes to warn that collections will be later than usual and moves non-urgent residents to the next visit day.

error.defect_description: A home is left off the re-assigned runs.

evidence.note: Common practice for mobile collection teams; share and times are estimates.

steps.name: Drive to the home
steps.description: The assistant drives the planned route to the next long-term care or retirement home with the cooler and supplies; travel between homes is shared across the residents collected at each home.

evidence.note: Mobile teams travel to facilities (dyn_hcp); per-resident share of 15 to 40 minutes of driving per home for 5 to 15 residents is an estimate.

steps.name: Check in at the nursing station and confirm the list
steps.description: The assistant signs in (with infection-control screening in 2020-2022), finds the charge nurse, and goes through the list: residents transferred to hospital, discharged or deceased are crossed off, new orders written since the list was printed are added, and the nurse confirms which residents are fasting and who needs help or is on isolation.

error.defect_description: A cancelled order is not crossed off, or a new order is missed.

next.condition: resident added from a new requisition at the home
resident in hospital, discharged, deceased or order cancelled

evidence.note: Residents are old and move between homes and hospital often (fao2019). Shares are estimates.

steps.name: Add an unscheduled resident
steps.description: For a new requisition the nurse hands over, the assistant checks it is signed and complete, phones the scheduling desk to have the order entered in the LIS or writes the details on a blank requisition with handwritten labels, and adds the resident to the round.

error.defect_description: Handwritten label or manual requisition error that accessioning must resolve.

evidence.note: Late orders from homes are named in the organisation file's scheduling process; handling at the home is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Identify the resident with nursing staff
steps.description: At the room the assistant matches the resident to the requisition using at least two identifiers, such as the name and date of birth on the medication record photo or wristband, confirmed by the nurse or personal support worker, because many residents cannot reliably state their own name.

error.defect_description: Wrong resident drawn, a serious error that may only show up in implausible results.

control.basis: Patient identification with two identifiers before collection, required by ISO 15189 and Institute for Quality Management in Healthcare (OLA) accreditation that Ontario licensing depends on

evidence.note: Two-identifier check (crl_instr); accreditation is a licensing condition (ag2017); 69 percent of residents have dementia (cihi_dementia). Times are estimates.

steps.name: Explain the draw and get the resident's cooperation
steps.description: The assistant explains the blood test to the resident, checks fasting status when the test requires it, and with a nurse or support worker calms residents who are anxious or agitated. A capable resident who refuses is not drawn; residents who are asleep, in the dining room or at therapy are left for later in the round.

control.basis: Health care consent law (Ontario Health Care Consent Act and equivalents): a capable person may refuse; a substitute decision-maker consents for an incapable resident

next.condition: refuses, agitated, asleep or away from the room
not fasting for a fasting test

evidence.note: A capable adult may refuse and substitute decision-makers act for incapable patients (cmpa_consent); half of residents with dementia show aggressive behaviour (cihi_dementia). Shares are estimates.

steps.name: Draw the blood
steps.description: The assistant draws the ordered tubes in the correct order, usually with a butterfly needle because elderly residents often have fragile, rolling veins, mixes each tube and applies pressure to prevent bruising. Policy allows two attempts before the draw is abandoned.

error.defect_description: Haemolysed, clotted or short-filled tube that the laboratory rejects.

next.condition: unable to draw after two attempts

evidence.note: Blood collection in homes (dyn_services); difficult-vein share and times are estimates for elderly residents.

steps.name: Label the tubes at the bedside
steps.description: Before leaving the resident, the assistant sticks the LIS barcode labels on each tube, writes the collection time and initials, and checks the labels against the requisition and the resident's identifiers.

error.defect_description: Tube mislabelled or unlabelled, rejected at accessioning and recollected.

control.basis: Specimen labelling at the point of collection in the patient's presence (ISO 15189 pre-examination requirements and OLA accreditation)

next.condition: nursing left urine or swab specimens for pick-up

evidence.note: Tubes labelled with the patient's name and barcodes at collection (dyn_kit2020); accreditation required for licensing (ag2017). Branch shares are estimates; ECG share follows the organisation file's 3,000 ECGs a month across mobile services.

steps.name: Pick up urine and swab specimens collected by nursing
steps.description: The assistant collects urine containers or swabs that nursing staff collected earlier for the resident, checks that each carries the resident's label and matches a requisition, and places them in the cooler bag.

error.defect_description: Unlabelled or unrefrigerated urine accepted, later rejected by the laboratory.

evidence.note: Collection of other specimens in homes is part of the service (dyn_hcp); share and times are estimates.

steps.name: Record and transmit a resting ECG
steps.description: The assistant positions the resident in bed, places the limb and chest electrodes, records a 12-lead tracing on the portable recorder, repeats it if movement spoils the trace, and transmits it with the resident's details to the reading service.

error.defect_description: Tracing with artifact or wrong patient details that the reading cardiologist returns.

evidence.note: Mobile ECG collections in long-term care and retirement homes (dyn_services, dyn_homecare); times are estimates.

steps.name: Document the collection
steps.description: The assistant ticks the resident off the list with the collection time, notes anything the laboratory should know (difficult draw, possible haemolysis, non-fasting), and writes a short note for the home's chart or the nurse that the collection was done.

error.defect_description: Collection time or non-fasting note left off, so results are misinterpreted.

evidence.note: Common practice; times are estimates.

steps.name: Process and pack the specimens
steps.description: After the home's round, the assistant lets serum tubes clot upright, spins them in a portable centrifuge where the run allows or plans delivery within the processing window, and packs tubes and requisitions in sealed biohazard bags in the cooler with cold packs.

error.defect_description: Tubes left too warm or too long before spinning, affecting potassium or glucose results.

control.basis: Laboratory specimen handling requirements (clotting, centrifuging within 2 to 4 hours, temperature) under the laboratory's accredited pre-examination procedures

evidence.note: Clot 30 minutes, centrifuge within 2 to 4 hours, keep cool at 2 to 8 C (dyn_kit2020, the company's insurance kit instructions, used here as an example of the same laboratory's handling rules). Times are estimates.

steps.name: Hand the specimens to the courier
steps.description: At the arranged time and place the assistant hands the cooler bags to the company courier, who scans them into the tracking system, or drops them at the nearest collection centre for the next route pick-up; ECG tracings were sent electronically.

error.defect_description: Bag missed by the courier and delivered late, past the stability limit.

control.basis: Transportation of Dangerous Goods rules for diagnostic specimens and laboratory transport standards (temperature and time)

evidence.note: Climate-controlled transport by TDG-certified couriers with scanning and tracking (dyn_logistics). The wait from draw to hand-off is an estimate.

steps.name: Return to the resident later in the round
steps.description: After the other residents in the home, the assistant goes back to residents who were asleep, away or refused, asks the nurse whether a second approach is appropriate and tries again.

evidence.note: Responsive behaviours vary through the day (cihi_dementia); success share is an estimate.

steps.name: Report a missed collection
steps.description: The assistant writes the reason on the requisition (refused, not fasting, unable to draw, unavailable), tells the nurse so the physician can be informed, and phones or texts the scheduling desk so the collection can be rebooked.

error.defect_description: Missed collection not reported, so the order silently lapses.

evidence.note: The organisation file names refusals, sleeping residents and non-fasting residents as causes of missed draws; reporting practice is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Record a cancelled collection
steps.description: For a resident who is in hospital, discharged, deceased or whose order the physician cancelled, the assistant marks the requisition cancelled with the reason so the scheduler can close or hold the order.

error.defect_description: Order closed although the resident returns from hospital the next day.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Reschedule the missed collection
steps.description: The scheduler records the missed reason in the LIS, books the resident for the home's next visit day or the next fasting slot, or holds the order if the home says the physician will review it, and confirms with the home.

error.defect_description: Rebooked on a day the home is not on the route.

next.condition: held or cancelled by the home or physician

evidence.note: Rescheduling is part of the organisation file's scheduling desk role; shares are estimates.

steps.name: Resolve a home's complaint about missed collections
steps.description: The regional manager calls the home's director of care, reviews the run records and the reasons for the misses, agrees changes such as an earlier fasting slot, a nurse assisting at the draw or a different assistant, and confirms the next collection.

control.basis: Service agreement with the home and complaint handling procedure

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Resident refuses, is agitated or unavailable
exceptions.description: The assistant returns later in the round; about half succeed and the rest are reported missed and rebooked.

exceptions.name: Unable to draw
exceptions.description: Fragile veins defeat two attempts; the miss is reported and rebooked, sometimes for a more experienced assistant.

exceptions.name: Not fasting
exceptions.description: The resident has eaten before a fasting test; the draw is rebooked for an early slot.

exceptions.name: Resident not in the home or order cancelled
exceptions.description: The resident is in hospital, discharged or deceased, or the physician cancelled the order.

exceptions.name: Order added at the home
exceptions.description: A new requisition is handed over at check-in and added to the round with the scheduling desk's help.

exceptions.name: Assistant absent
exceptions.description: The team lead redistributes the absent assistant's homes and collections run late.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the schedule being issued (afternoon before) to specimens handed to the courier
benchmarks.population: Mobile long-term care collections, Ontario and Manitoba, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Synthesis: schedules are built the afternoon before for early-morning runs and specimens must reach processing within a few hours (centrifuge within 2 to 4 hours in the company's kit instructions); missed draws move to the next visit day. No published distribution was found.
Explains why staff help with identification and why refusals are common.

pain_points.description: Residents with dementia refuse or are agitated, and residents asleep or away from their rooms must be revisited, so a share of draws is missed and rebooked.

evidence.note: 69 percent of residents have dementia and half of those show aggressive behaviour (cihi_dementia); capable residents may refuse (cmpa_consent).

pain_points.description: Fragile veins in elderly residents lead to failed or haemolysed draws.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Lists printed the afternoon before go out of date overnight as residents go to hospital or new orders are written, causing rework at check-in.

evidence.note: Author's estimate based on the organisation file's description of late orders and changes from homes.

pain_points.description: Specimens must reach processing within a few hours, so runs are tied to courier meeting times and missed hand-offs risk rejected specimens.

evidence.note: Centrifuge within 2 to 4 hours and keep cool (dyn_kit2020); temperature-controlled courier network (dyn_logistics).

pain_points.description: Waiting for the charge nurse during the morning medication pass and infection-control screening in 2020-2022 add unproductive time at each home.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

sources.title: Services
sources.supports: The model laboratory Mobile Services recruits certified health professionals to perform mobile blood and ECG collections in long-term care and retirement homes, plus private house call visits.

sources.title: Healthcare provider solutions
sources.supports: The company visits patients in long-term care facilities, homes and workplaces to collect specimens; mobile teams perform blood draws and ECGs; a specialised logistics team handles delivery timing, storage and compliance; results go electronically to EMRs and the eResults portal.

sources.title: Home care
sources.supports: Mobile lab work and ECGs at home or office in Ontario and Winnipeg, booked by phone, fax or requisition upload; mobile blood and ECG collections in long-term care and retirement homes by certified health professionals.

sources.title: The model laboratory Logistics
sources.supports: Climate-controlled transport of specimens; all team members hold Transportation of Dangerous Goods certification; quality metrics such as Ontario Laboratory Accreditation standards; 24/7 dispatch; web-based tracking of shipments.

sources.title: Instructions for blood/urine kit (insurance)
sources.supports: Company collection instructions: label tubes with the patient's name and barcodes at collection; SST tube clots upright 30 minutes and should be centrifuged within 2 to 4 hours; keep samples cool and refrigerated at 2 to 8 C until courier pick-up; sharps never shipped with specimens.

sources.title: Insurance collections: specific instructions for examiners
sources.supports: Confirm the person's identity by checking at least two identifiers before collecting; refrigerate specimens that cannot be shipped the same day.

sources.title: Laboratory services in the health sector (Annual Report 2017, section 3.07)
sources.publisher: Office of the Auditor General of Ontario
sources.supports: Laboratory services run from requisition to specimen collection, analysis and result reporting; under the Laboratory and Specimen Collection Centre Licensing Act community laboratories and collection centres must be licensed and must take part in the Institute for Quality Management in Healthcare accreditation and proficiency testing program to stay licensed.

sources.title: Long-Term Care Homes Program: a review of the plan to create 15,000 new long-term care beds in Ontario
sources.supports: 626 long-term care homes in Ontario house over 78,000 residents; 78,664 beds in operation in 2018-19; over 80 percent of residents are over 75.

sources.title: Dementia in long-term care
sources.supports: 69 percent of long-term care residents had dementia in 2015-2016, and half of residents with dementia showed some aggressive behaviour (Aggressive Behaviour Scale of 1 or more).

sources.title: Consent: a guide for Canadian physicians
sources.supports: A capable adult may refuse treatment or investigations; a substitute decision-maker ranked by provincial law consents for an incapable patient; refusals should be documented.

sources.title: Wages: Medical laboratory technical assistant in Ontario (NOC 33101)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low 17.95, median 26.25, high 36.00 dollars (Labour Force Survey 2023-2024).

assumptions: Steps done once per home or per run (preparing, driving, checking in, packing, hand-off) are shown per resident with a share of the time, assuming 5 to 15 residents per home and 15 to 25 residents per run.

Refusal, unavailability, failed-draw and cancellation shares are estimates; no published rates for long-term care collections were found. Overall about 9 percent of scheduled collections are missed and 4 percent cancelled.

Handling limits (clot 30 minutes, centrifuge within 2 to 4 hours, 2 to 8 C) come from the company's insurance kit instructions and are assumed to reflect the same laboratory's handling rules for community specimens.
Identification and labelling controls rest on ISO 15189 and Ontario's IQMH accreditation, which licensing requires; the exact clauses were not opened.
The Ontario long-term care regulation that requires homes to arrange laboratory services could not be opened and is not cited.
Mobile lab assistant FTE (88 of 120) leaves about 30 for house calls (2,500 a month) and training, which is tight; loaded costs come from the organisation file (hourly wage times 1.35).
